summary: Both sides are alive, sensor-driven and beat-locked with the same AGC-to-dim-field arc and near-identical steady-state mean brightness, but the port draws a smooth spatially-coherent blob/ring field where the original draws per-pixel-independent hard-clipped speckle, and the port's palette rotates ~3.6x too fast.
observations: Rig/setup: default rig is a 16x16 grid (256 px). Neither side exposes ANY control (probe.json: 'no settable controls' on both) - control surfaces match exactly. Output is seed-independent: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give identical statsSummary on both sides (mean 12 orig / 14 port at --skip 30 --seconds 10 --fps 20).

Both sides report wantsSensors:true and were fed sensorModel beat120 on every run. With --sensors off both render EXACTLY black (mean 0, motion 0 over a 10 s / 20 fps window) - identical graceful-degradation behaviour, no divergence there.

BEAT LOCK (both correct): at 20 fps in steady state both sides attack every 10 frames = 0.5 s = the 2 Hz beat, then decay across the interval. Orig meanBrightness (skip 20, 20 fps, frames 0-60): 3 5 5 4 3 3 2 2 2 1 1 | 31 30 22 19 18 16 15 14 13 12 11 ... - attacks at frames 11, 31, 41. Port: 8 18 16 14 11 9 8 7 6 5 4 | 19 18 15 13 11 10 9 7 6 6 | 53 50 44 ... - attacks at frames 11, 21, 31, 41, 51. Both rhythm PNGs show clean horizontal beat banding.

STRUCTURE - the headline divergence. ORIGINAL IS INDEX-ONLY: its flat pixel sequence at t=24 s is byte-identical (mean abs diff 0.00) across a 16x16 grid, a 32x8 grid and a 256-px strip. PORT IS COORDINATE-DRIVEN on grids: 16x16 vs 32x8 differ by mean abs 41.9 per pixel at the same instant (187 of 256 pixels differ by >2). (Curiosity: the port's 16x16-grid frame IS byte-identical to its 256-px-strip frame, so only the non-square grid separates them.)

The original's flat sequence is EXACTLY periodic with period 196 px (= 14x14) and that period does not scale with rig size: best-repeat scan gives 196:0.00 on a 256-px rig and 196:0.00 / 392:0.00 on a 600-px rig. So the original has a fixed 196-cell native unit repeated along the pixel index. The port has no such exact period (best 25:22.8 at 600 px, i.e. noise-floor).

Visually that means: original = spatially UNCORRELATED confetti/speckle - individual pixels snap on at full 255 and fade, neighbours unrelated. Port = smooth, spatially COHERENT field - the baseline sheet at 0.0 s is a soft green/red blob field, and steady-state frames show closed rings, arcs and long diagonal streaks (clearly visible in steady20/port.png and port-motion.png at 24.0-24.25 s, where a green ring persists and fades as one object). Confirmed from --dump numbers, not just images: at t=30.55 s the port's high values (255, 244, 223, 222, 213, 206, 154...) are all clustered in rows 7-14 / cols 9-15, while the original's 255s are scattered across all 16 rows.

Rendering both on the original's native 14x14 (196 px) geometry does NOT make the original resolve into spectrum columns - it is still scattered speckle (grid14/orig.png). So the speckle look is the pattern's real appearance, not a reshaping artefact of the 16x16 default rig.

DYNAMIC RANGE: over 18 dumped steady-state frames on the default rig, orig has 52.1% pure-black pixels, 4.75% fully saturated (up to 42 of 256 pixels at 255 on a strong beat), mean channel-max 26.8. Port has 31.7% black, 0.26% saturated (max 8 pixels in one frame), mean channel-max 20.2. The original hard-clips on beats; the port is a softer, more continuous haze with far fewer black pixels.

Spatial smoothness corroborates: mean |neighbour delta| along the flat index is 38.5 (orig) vs 26.9 (port); along a column 43.5 (orig) vs 27.4 (port). The port's field is ~30% smoother in both directions and near-isotropic (ratio 0.98 vs orig's 0.89).

PALETTE ROTATION RATE: unwrapped hue of the mean colour over a 40 s steady window at 20 fps travels 1112 deg / 36 s = 30.9 deg/s on the original (full hue cycle ~11.7 s) vs 4399 deg / 40 s = 110.1 deg/s on the port (full cycle ~3.27 s). The port's palette walk is ~3.6x too fast. Both walk in the same direction and cover the full rainbow, so it is a rate error, not a palette-family error.

SUPER-CYCLE: orig motion autocorrelation peaks at 30 frames = 1.5 s at 20 fps (harmonics 60, 90); port peaks at 40 frames = 2.0 s (harmonics 80, 120, 160), i.e. an exact 4-beat cycle. The port's 2.0 s super-cycle is stable at every rate tested (20f@10fps, 40f@20fps, 80f@40fps = 2.0 s each); the original's wanders with fps (2.5 s @10, 1.5 s @20, 1.0 s @40) and is less regular. Port autocorrelation is also much stronger (0.86 peak vs 0.63), i.e. the port repeats itself more mechanically than the original.

AGC WARM-UP TRANSIENT differs in shape and in what it is clocked on. Original: railed at 255 from frame 0 and decays monotonically (1 s moving avg at 20 fps: 199 183 155 132 115 95 92 86 84 82 79 75 67 57 47 37 27 17 9 -> settles ~9-12). Port: starts DIM (27 at frame 0), ramps UP to 255 by frame ~4, holds railed to ~frame 25, then crashes (238 255 253 249 237 212 173 125 77 41 18 8 4 3 2 -> near-black at frames ~65-75) before recovering to ~13. The port's overshoot-then-near-blackout undershoot is not in the original.

The transient's clock differs too. Time for the 1 s moving average to first fall below 2x the settled level: orig 94 / 83 / 66 frames at 10 / 20 / 40 fps (= 9.4 / 4.15 / 1.65 s) - roughly FRAME-counted; port 35 / 48 / 116 frames (= 3.5 / 2.4 / 2.9 s) - roughly TIME-based. The original's settle point therefore moves with fps and the port's does not, so the two only line up at one rate. (Note: in STEADY state both sides are frame-rate-sensitive to a similar degree - the same absolute instant rendered at 20 vs 40 fps differs by mean abs 31.9 on orig and 28.1 on port - so this is a transient-clock finding, not a general frame-coupling finding.)

Settled brightness levels are close and get closer at higher fps: settled 1 s-avg brightness orig 9.4 / 11.4 / 15.0 vs port 12.2 / 13.6 / 15.2 at 10 / 20 / 40 fps. Overall port runs ~20-30% brighter in steady state at 20 fps (60 s survey at 10 fps: orig avg 23.5, port avg 22.8; 8 s steady window at 20 fps: orig 11, port 14).

Motion magnitude: orig motion avg 10.9 vs port 5.5 over the 6 s baseline, and 7.2 vs 4.5 over the 60 s / 10 fps survey - the original changes roughly 1.6-2x harder frame to frame, consistent with its hard on/off speckle vs the port's smooth fades. zeroMotionFrames over the 6 s baseline: orig 7, port 30.
feedback: The single biggest fix: the port must drive pixels from the PIXEL INDEX only, not from (x,y). Proof of the original's behaviour: its flat output is byte-identical on a 16x16 grid, a 32x8 grid and a 256-px strip, and the flat sequence repeats EXACTLY every 196 pixels (14x14) regardless of rig size (verified at 256 and 600 px). The port currently changes completely between 16x16 and 32x8. Result on screen: the original is uncorrelated confetti, the port draws rings, arcs and diagonal streaks. Target: neighbouring pixels should be independent, and re-rendering on any rig shape should give the same flat sequence.

Reproduce the 196-cell native unit. Whatever cell table the original uses, it has exactly 196 entries and is indexed with a wrap (index mod 196), so a 256-px rig shows one full unit plus a 60-px repeat of its head. A quick regression: dump one steady-state frame on a 600-px strip and check the best flat-repeat period is 196 with mean abs diff 0.00.

Restore the dynamic range. The original hard-clips: on a strong beat 16% of pixels (42/256) hit 255 and 52% sit at pure 0. The port peaks around 75-255 only rarely (0.26% saturated) and leaves only 32% black, giving a hazy look. Push the per-cell gain up and let it clip, and make un-triggered cells decay all the way to 0.

Slow the palette walk by ~3.6x. Measured on the mean colour over a 40 s steady window at 20 fps: original 30.9 deg/s (full hue cycle ~11.7 s), port 110.1 deg/s (~3.27 s). Same direction, same full-rainbow range - only the rate is wrong.

Loosen the super-cycle. The port locks to a clean 4-beat (2.0 s) repeat at every frame rate with autocorrelation 0.86; the original's strongest lag is 1.5 s at 20 fps with only 0.63 correlation and it shifts with fps. The port is repeating a fixed 4-beat template where the original keeps re-randomizing; per-beat cell selection should not repeat on a 2 s loop.

Fix the AGC warm-up shape. Original starts RAILED at 255 on frame 0 and decays monotonically to its settled level over ~80 frames at 20 fps, with only a shallow undershoot (dips to 9, recovers to ~12). The port starts dim (27), overshoots up to 255 by frame 4, holds railed ~25 frames, then crashes to near-black (1 s avg of 2 at frames 65-75) before recovering. Remove the initial ramp-in and the deep blackout undershoot.

The AGC time constant is on the wrong clock. The original's settle point is roughly FRAME-counted (94/83/66 frames to fall below 2x settled at 10/20/40 fps); the port's is roughly TIME-based (3.5/2.4/2.9 s). Drive the gain smoother off a per-render-frame count, not off elapsed seconds, so the transient length tracks the original at every frame rate.

Things that are already right and should not be disturbed: both sides are beat-locked at exactly 2 Hz (attack every 10 frames at 20 fps) with a per-beat hold-and-fade; both render exactly black with --sensors off; both are seed-independent; steady-state mean brightness is within ~20-30% and converges at 40 fps; control surfaces match (neither side has any control).
